title: I Told the Group Chat I Would Not Host Thanksgiving Again

parts.text: I typed I am not hosting and watched the chat go feral in three minutes. I am forty-one, teacher, owner of the big table by accident of floor plan. For six years I cooked, they arrived late, they left dishes in artistic stacks. The gravy boat still has a chip from Uncle Craig. The kitchen smelled like sage even in July, a trauma perfume. My sister Leah said tradition. I said tradition is not unpaid catering. Mom said I was destroying the holiday. I sent a link to a restaurant with a private room and a split check. Three people loved it. Two people called me cold. We ate at the restaurant. The mashed potatoes were worse. I was happier. I bought a small pie for my apartment and ate it in socks. The chip in the gravy boat is now a paperclip holder. I will visit. I will not be the venue. The chat is quieter, which I enjoy like a nap. Leah said, "So that's it, tradition's dead" I said, "Tradition can Uber" Nate did the dishes at the restaurant tip jar with cash. That was new. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened.

social.video_title: I refused to host Thanksgiving and sent a restaurant link
social.description: Sage trauma perfume, a chipped gravy boat, split checks. The potatoes were worse. I was happier. Would you have hosted year seven?
